title: Road to sudo
briefing: 09:58, your pager screams. PROD-01, the box that runs everything, is at
100% CPU. Read ~/INCIDENT.txt. Nothing else will be explained.
This is everything, all at once.
expert_briefing: PROD-01 down. You have sudo. Fix it. Take root.
tips: Investigate with ps aux. A root-owned process needs root to stop it: `sudo -i` opens a root shell.
You've earned sudo. `sudo -i` makes you root; the prompt turns to #.
objective: Investigate PROD-01, take root, and stop the rogue root-owned process that's melting the server.
expert_objective: Restore PROD-01. End the rogue root process. Hold the throne.
hints: Find what's eating the CPU: `ps aux` (or `top`). It runs as root, so you can't kill it as yourself.
Become root — you're trusted with it: `sudo -i`. The prompt turns to root@prod-01:~#.
As root, kill the rogue process by its PID (ps shows it): `sudo -i`, then `kill 1313`.

reactions.say: Permission denied — that process belongs to root, and so must you, for a moment. Try `sudo -i`.

explanation:
YOU MADE IT.

Welcome to the other side of the prompt.

You walked in as a user who didn't know their own name, and walked out having taken root on a burning production server — the honest way, by understanding the system well enough to hold its most dangerous prompt. That's what sudo really is: not power, but responsibility you earned.
